\exfigure{323_q16_s2}

In right-angled $\triangle TSB$, $\angle STB=42^\circ$:

$$\begin{aligned} \tan 42^\circ&=\dfrac{SB}{50}\\ SB&=50\tan 42^\circ \end{aligned}$$

In right-angled $\triangle TDB$, $\angle DTB=55^\circ$:

$$\begin{aligned} \tan 55^\circ&=\dfrac{BD}{50}\\ BD&=50\tan 55^\circ \end{aligned}$$

Cosine rule in $\triangle SBD$ with $\angle SBD=62^\circ$:

$$\begin{aligned} SD^2&=(50\tan 55^\circ)^2+(50\tan 42^\circ)^2-2(50\tan 55^\circ)(50\tan 42^\circ)\cos 62^\circ\\ &=4107.3439\ldots\\ SD&=\sqrt{4107.3439\ldots}\\ \therefore SD&=64.09 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} u&=\ln(x-1) & v&=x-1\\ u'&=\dfrac{1}{x-1} & v'&=1 \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} y'&=\dfrac{(x-1)\left(\frac{1}{x-1}\right)-\ln(x-1)(1)}{(x-1)^2}\\ &=\dfrac{1-\ln(x-1)}{(x-1)^2} \end{aligned}$$

Substitute $x=2$:

$$\begin{aligned} y'&=\dfrac{1-\ln(2-1)}{(2-1)^2}\\ &=1-\ln 1\\ &=1 \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} \int_0^a \big(3t^2-6t+4-(6t+4)\big)\,dt&=0\\ \int_0^a (3t^2-12t)\,dt&=0\\ \Big[t^3-6t^2\Big]_0^a&=0\\ a^3-6a^2&=0\\ a^2(a-6)&=0\\ a&=0,\ 6 \end{aligned}$$

The total probability is 1:

$$\begin{aligned} \int_0^2 f(x)\,dx&=1\\ \int_0^2 \dfrac{kx}{5-x^2}\,dx&=1\\ -\dfrac{k}{2}\int_0^2 \dfrac{-2x}{5-x^2}\,dx&=1\\ -\dfrac{k}{2}\Big[\ln|5-x^2|\Big]_0^2&=1\\ -\dfrac{k}{2}\big[\ln|5-4|-\ln|5-0|\big]&=1\\ -\dfrac{k}{2}\big[\ln 1-\ln 5\big]&=1\\ -\dfrac{k}{2}(0-\ln 5)&=1\\ \dfrac{k\ln 5}{2}&=1\\ k&=\dfrac{2}{\ln 5} \end{aligned}$$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 2: Correct answer; 1: Sets up $\displaystyle\int_0^2 \dfrac{kx}{5-x^2}\,dx=1$ with a correct primitive, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
For $0\le x\le 2$:

$$\begin{aligned} F(x)&=\int_0^x \dfrac{2}{\ln 5}\left(\dfrac{x}{5-x^2}\right)dx\\ &=-\dfrac{1}{\ln 5}\int_0^x \dfrac{-2x}{5-x^2}\,dx\\ &=-\dfrac{1}{\ln 5}\Big[\ln|5-x^2|\Big]_0^x\\ &=\dfrac{1}{\ln 5}\big[\ln|5|-\ln|5-x^2|\big]\\ &=1-\dfrac{\ln|5-x^2|}{\ln 5} \end{aligned}$$

Applying the change of base rule, $\log_a b=\dfrac{\ln b}{\ln a}$:

$$\begin{aligned} F(x)&=1-\log_5|5-x^2|\\ &=1-\log_5(5-x^2) \end{aligned}$$

since $5-x^2>0$ for $0\le x\le 2$. $F(x)=0$ for $x<0$ and $F(x)=1$ for $x>2$.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 2: Correct answer; 1: Correct integral with a correct primitive, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
The median $m$ satisfies $F(m)=0.5$:

$$\begin{aligned} 1-\log_5(5-x^2)&=0.5\\ \log_5(5-x^2)&=0.5\\ 5-x^2&=5^{0.5}\\ 5-x^2&=\sqrt{5}\\ x^2&=5-\sqrt{5}\\ x&=\pm\sqrt{5-\sqrt{5}} \end{aligned}$$

$\therefore x=\sqrt{5-\sqrt{5}}$, since $0\le x\le 2$.

For $0\le t\le 24$, $-\dfrac{5\pi}{2}\le\dfrac{\pi}{6}(t-15)\le\dfrac{3\pi}{2}$:

From the graph, the satellite is above 11 000 km for $4<t<8$ and $16<t<20$.

For an inflection point, $f''(x)=0$:

$$\begin{aligned} 6x+6&=0\\ x&=-1 \end{aligned}$$

$f(-1)=1$, so $(-1,1)$ is a possible inflection point. Check concavity:

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c} x & -2 & -1 & 0\\ \hline f''(x) & -6 & 0 & 6 \end{array}$$

There is a change in concavity, $\therefore (-1,1)$ is an inflection point.

solutions.latex:
Initially $C=0$. Since $k>0$, $2^{-kt}\to 0$ as $t\to\infty$, so $C\to 100$ as $t\to\infty$.

$$\begin{aligned} C'&=100k\ln 2\times 2^{-kt}\\ C''&=-100k^2(\ln 2)^2\times 2^{-kt} \end{aligned}$$

Since $k>0$, $C'>0$ and $C''<0$ for all $t\ge 0$.

Hence, the battery charge capacity increases from 0 at a decreasing rate over time, but can never reach $100\%$ charge.
